hypothesis: A timed-out generation's same-turn usage, observed only after an independent task-score receipt, projects into the standard measured-run adapter as complete attempt tokens. With the same timeout and score but no usage receipt, totals remain incomplete and cannot qualify matched break-even.
treatment: Synthetic timeout attempt with a hash-bound App Server usage JSONL row; record an UNKNOWN independent score; invoke the public caller's explicit post-score observe_late_usage; reconcile and project with build_measured_run.
control: Identical synthetic timeout attempt and UNKNOWN score, with a late-usage source that returns no row; reconcile and project the same way.
dose: One run per condition, no retries, no public Relay calls, no GUI or OS input, no provider/model call, no Docker or WSLc allocation.
decision_rule: PASS only if treatment reports input=18 and output=3 with complete usage while control reports incomplete usage and null input/output totals; both scores must remain UNKNOWN, Relay calls must be zero, and all raw references must hash-verify. Any mismatch is retained as a failure.
schema_note: The comparator requires effect_attribution fields. Both runs use null effect_observed_ns and synthetic monotonic envelope values solely to satisfy this schema. They are not input release, authority, or task-effect evidence.
scope: Synthetic accounting composition only. This does not test provider delivery/billing, task effect, live caller scheduling, matched A/B/C economics, or recovery reliability.
interpreter: Windows CPython 3.11 (py -3.11), run normally and with -O
